identityReview: Lassina Zerbo, Burkinabe geophysicist and diplomat, reported birth 10 October 1963. Paris XI doctorate confirmed across profiles but year conflicts (1992 versus 1993), so public year omitted. IDC director 2004–2013; third CTBTO Preparatory Commission executive secretary 1 August 2013–31 July 2021; Burkina Faso prime minister appointed 10 December 2021, cabinet formed 13 December, parliamentary investiture 7 January 2022, ended with 24 January coup. Rwanda board chair reported already in October 2021; 2024 presidential adviser appointment and current chairmanship are distinct from agency CEO.
lifeStatusEvidence: A 1 November 2026 retrospective reports that he actually moderated the 28 October nuclear-technology panel in Moscow, with substantive remarks and current identification as Rwanda Atomic Energy Board chairman and presidential adviser. This is a completed appearance, not merely a speaker announcement. No later physical appearance is inferred from reused quotations in November coverage.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read selected institutional biographies, CTBTO Secretariat and treaty overview, Nature profile, Burkina government review and policy-declaration PDF excerpts, Anadolu vote report, Reuters coup report, Rwanda gazette appointment provisions, RAEB board page, Rosatom release, WNN reporting and Rwanda Inspirer retrospective. Read Commons licence/history without original pixels. Source-specific scope and conflicts are recorded below.
corrections: Read the 10 December 2021 appointment and biographical paragraphs. They report the same-day presidential appointment, replacement of Christophe Dabire, 10 October 1963 birth and Paris XI geophysics doctorate. Much of the biography links to translated Wikipedia and is not independent primary authentication. The current-executive-secretary wording was already stale by December 2021; do not copy it. Exact birth date is corroborated by search-indexed Actualite and OCLC entries, whose full relevant bodies were unavailable, not by a civil register. Avoid unverified birth-place precision. Degree year 1993 is not retained publicly because other read CVs give 1992.

Read the short WEF biography: Paris XI geophysics doctorate listed as 1993, BHP then Anglo American, and International Data Centre directorship 2004–2013. Its since-2013 executive-secretary heading is historical, not proof of current office. It describes scientific conferences, tsunami-warning cooperation and the virtual Data Exploitation Centre. Public text does not conflate responsibility for a data centre with founding the entire monitoring system. The BHP starting-year detail conflicts with the more detailed RTB/Sidwaya CV and is omitted.

Read the ELN education and career paragraphs: Burkinabe nationality, Paris XI geophysics PhD in 1993, earlier IDC leadership and monitoring assistance relating to DPRK tests, Fukushima and tsunami warnings. The profile still presents him as incumbent CTBTO head and includes 2013 conference responsibilities; it is used for historical career, not November 2026 office. No doctorate certificate or thesis was accessed. Public degree year is omitted because read national CVs disagree.

Read the Sidwaya education and detailed-career excerpts. The article itself is internally inconsistent: narrative says doctorate in 1993, appended CV says 1992. Public text states the degree and institution without choosing a year by majority vote. CV gives IDC November 2004–July 2013, executive secretary 1 August 2013–31 July 2021, emeritus in July 2021 and Rwanda board chair from October 2021. Therefore the Rwanda chairmanship was not necessarily first obtained after the January 2022 coup. No exact first board-appointment decree was reviewed. Retain only the year 2004 for IDC entry, and no exact BHP joining year. Promotional claims and honorary titles are not substituted for earned degrees.

Read the CTBTO official Provisional Technical Secretariat history. It explicitly gives Zerbo as third executive secretary from 1 August 2013 and Robert Floyd as fourth from 1 August 2021. The executive secretary is appointed by and reports to the Preparatory Commission. This is not UN secretary-general or leadership of an already fully operational post-entry-into-force treaty organization. The Secretariat page was accessible even though several separate historical CTBTO news pages returned 403.

Read the official treaty overview, including the 1996 Preparatory Commission resolution, present non-entry-into-force statement, and Article XIV/Annex 2 requirements. Distinguish a functioning preparatory monitoring system from entry into force of the CTBT and its eventual legal verification regime. Do not claim Zerbo achieved universal ratification, the treaty entered into force, or an on-site exercise was an authorized inspection of an actual nuclear test.

Read the Lassina Zerbo section of Nature’s 2017 annual feature, not every other profile. It describes the 3 September DPRK test, his exchanges with diplomats, the international monitoring network, scientific data sharing and treaty advocacy. His comments and outside praise are attributed perspectives, not a quantified causal evaluation. Nature’s 10 is an editorial personalities feature, not a Nobel Prize or a research degree. Older station counts and geopolitical statements are not used as current 2026 figures.

Read the relevant pages of the government bimonthly review hosted by RTB: appointment on 10 December 2021, new government formed on 13 December and security/state-authority priorities. Appointment, formation and parliamentary investiture are separate events. The review’s cabinet-size description differs from Anadolu’s counting; public text omits the count rather than silently treating different inclusion conventions as identical. Government advocacy and operational security claims in other sections were not independently audited or adopted.

Read the cover, opening and four-priority section of the 7 January 2022 general policy declaration, plus relevant governance paragraphs. It prioritizes peace/security and resilience, return of internally displaced people, reconciliation, and anti-corruption/illicit-enrichment work. The published document says only the delivered speech is authoritative; no audio/video comparison was performed. Commitments in a policy address are not demonstrated outcomes. This PDF is not itself the parliamentary voting record.

Read Anadolu’s 8 January 2022 retrospective report of the Friday evening investiture: 103 yes, 24 abstentions, zero no out of 127. Pair with the 7 January dated policy declaration to establish event day, rather than using next-day publication. The report incorrectly calls him 59, inconsistent with the reported October 1963 birth at that date; no age is copied. Its physicist shorthand is rendered as geophysicist using the educational biographies. Not a new first appointment on 7 or 8 January.

Read Reuters’ 24 January 2022 opening and relevant coup paragraphs via Investing.com: army ousted President Kabore and announced suspension of the constitution and dissolution of government/parliament. The military’s justification is its account, not independent endorsement or democratic authorization. Contemporaneous uncertainty about Kabore’s location or detention is not evidence that Zerbo personally was held in the same circumstances. Public text does not adopt unverified arrest/release detail or confuse this coup with the later September 2022 coup.

Read Presidential Order 071/01 in the 28 August 2024 special Official Gazette, especially English/French appointment and Article 4 (printed pages 62–64). It appoints Zerbo energy adviser and member of the Strategy and Policy Council in the Office of the President. The order enters into force on gazette publication and takes effect from 22 May 2024, the cited cabinet decision. Public timeline uses the effect date and explains later publication; neither is treated as the first Rwanda board chairmanship. Read those provisions only, not all 7825 extracted lines or the Kinyarwanda legal text.

Read the Rwanda Atomic Energy Board board page. It names Zerbo energy adviser to the President and chairman, and separately lists Fidele Ndahao as CEO. This confirms institutional distinction rather than making Zerbo CEO or a Rwandan national. The page has an internally awkward sentence about serving within the organization before joining it; that wording is not copied. Generic praise is not independent evaluation of nuclear safety or programme success.

Read the 30 June 2026 Rosatom/Atom Media release describing the completed Moscow Joint Coordinating Committee meeting, co-chairing with Kirill Komarov, SMR roadmap and workforce/regulatory/scientific cooperation. The release is a participant’s account. It supports a June event with contemporary WNN reporting; no exact meeting day is inferred from publication. The research-reactor proposal and early-2030s nuclear-power aspiration are plans, not proof of licensed construction, financing completion or operation.

Read the opening and quoted planning sections of WNN’s 1 July 2026 report. It describes the coordination meeting and roadmap as completed, supporting June rather than the contradictory July dateline in a Rwanda-government repost. WNN is a nuclear-industry publication using participant information, not an independent regulator’s project certification. The read section describes future plans; no reactor has been declared operational on that basis.

Read Rwanda Inspirer’s 1 November 2026 report of the 28 October Moscow panel during the third Russia–Africa Summit business programme. It reports completed moderation by Zerbo as RAEB chairman/presidential adviser and substantive discussion of training, infrastructure and cooperation. This supports recent life/activity and current roles; 1 November is publication, not event day. The article is closely aligned with Rosatom communications, so industry promotion, Africa-wide construction rhetoric and future targets are not independent evidence of a functioning Rwanda reactor. The retrospective explicitly locates the first joint committee meeting in June 2026.

additionalConsulted.access: Read scientific/career and education excerpts. Doctorate listed 1992, BHP 1994–1995, IDC November 2004–July 2013. The claim of still serving as executive secretary in December 2021 is stale. Its doctorate discrepancy is retained in review, not silently erased.

Read substantive text: header 30 June 2026 but body dateline 29 July 2026. This is an unresolved internal date error. Contemporary 30 June Rosatom release, 1 July WNN completed-event report and later June retrospective support June; do not use 29 July or infer exact 29 June meeting day.

Read Czech mission’s 23 May 2021 report: Floyd elected 21 May and due to succeed Zerbo 1 August. Scheduled succession is confirmed by the current CTBTO Secretariat history; May election is not August accession.
Search indexed 23 October 2012 selection; full opening returned 403. Public actual-start date relies on accessible official Secretariat history, not a claimed full reading of this release.
Search indexed honorary title, two terms and planned 1 August 2021 succession; full opening 403. Do not describe full-body review or make emeritus title an ongoing executive office.
Search indexed Bobo-Dioulasso and 1963 birth; opening 403. Public facts omit unverified birthplace detail and do not import the article’s imprecise UN-organization description.
Search excerpt gives 10 October 1963 and PhD 1993; opening 403. Excerpt corroboration only, not independent original identity/degree records.
Search index gave exact 1963-10-10 date; opened page returned no relevant birth text and find had no match. Do not claim the date was read in the live body.
Search indexed 17 November 2026 story with a reused Zerbo quote from the Russia–Africa Summit. Not used as evidence of his personal attendance in Antalya on 12–13 November.
Read caption, CC BY 2.0 terms, successful 2013 Flickr licence-review notice and sole displayed file-history entry. No image pixels inspected.
Original-source link returned 403; current Flickr body/terms unavailable. Commons archived licence-review notice read.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial/translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No civil birth record, original doctorate certificate/thesis, full parliamentary minutes, complete 2022 government-performance evaluation, original first Rwanda board-appointment decree, regulator-approved reactor completion record, event video or portrait pixels reviewed. Preserve degree-year uncertainty and date distinctions; policy promises and industry statements are not independently verified outcomes.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English: Burkinabe nationality versus Rwanda office; geophysics degree with year omitted; Preparatory Commission/Provisional Technical Secretariat versus post-entry-into-force organization and UN secretary-general; IDC versus entire institution; 2013–2021 tenure; December appointment/cabinet formation versus January parliamentary vote and coup; 2024 adviser effective date versus August promulgation and earlier chairmanship; board chair versus CEO; June meeting rather than erroneous July dateline; October event versus November report; nuclear-power goals versus operational reactors.
